key_insight: Forcing-informed resolvent analysis learns the input and output subspaces directly from flow data so the extracted forcing-response modes and gains match the actual self-sustained dynamics of nonlinear unsteady flows.
engineering_relevance: This provides a more physically faithful, data-driven tool for diagnosing and modeling flow amplification, mode coupling, and energy transfer in CFD surrogates and reduced-order models.
method: Estimate input and output bases from forcing and response snapshots.
Build a forcing-informed resolvent operator using these data-derived subspaces.
Use a nonlinear energy transfer map to locate where forcing injects or removes fluctuation energy.
evidence_signal: The framework is validated on the Stuart-Landau oscillator and demonstrated on a 2D cylinder wake and a 3D transitional boundary layer, recovering gains and paired modes even at frequencies dominated by nonlinear amplification.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on having representative simulation data for the forcing and response subspaces, so incomplete or noisy snapshots may weaken the extracted modes and operator.
paper_title: Forcing-informed resolvent analysis: Identification of input-output relations in self-sustained flows
